tagline: Up Lynx Creek to an old gold camp in the pines.
intro: Walker Road leaves Highway 69 and follows Lynx Creek up into the Bradshaw Mountains, under ponderosa pine the whole way. The first half is Prescott National Forest, with campgrounds and Lynx Lake. The second half is cabins and houses on land cut from the old mining claims. At the place called the 100 mailboxes the pavement ends. The road goes on unpaved toward Mount Union.
Joseph Walker's party panned this creek in 1863. One of them shot a lynx nearby, and the creek kept the name. By the 1930s it had given up more placer gold than any other stream bed in Arizona.

moments.title: Lynx Lake
moments.text: Arizona Game and Fish dammed Lynx Creek here, six miles below Walker, and a 2.5-mile trail loops the shore of the 55-acre lake.

moments.title: Smelter Hill
moments.text: Near the hill stood Howell's, a smelter town of 1882, now a ghost town site. The pavement reached the bottom of the hill in 1967.

moments.title: Walker
moments.text: A mining camp at about 6,289 feet that faded with its mines in the early 1900s, lost much of itself to fire in 1909 and closed its post office in 1940.

practical: The designated road is paved for about 7.5 miles; beyond the 100 mailboxes Walker Road continues unpaved.
